prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: c1ccc(-c2cnn[nH]2)cc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL4685

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant IDO expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 AI
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant N-terminal His-tagged IDO1 (Ala2 to Gly403) overexpressed in Escherichia coli BL21 at pH 6.5 after 60 mins by HPLC analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO", "confidence": 0.5, "error_class": "other", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for IDO1 inhibition using recombinant human protein expressed in E. coli, but differences in construct (His-tagged truncation vs. full-length), pH conditions (pH 6.5 explicitly stated in B), and detection method (HPLC vs. unspecified) could shift IC50 values in either direction, making it uncertain whether results will agree within 0.3 log units or diverge beyond 1.0 log units."}
